summary: Conservation policy sets an EU-wide LULUCF carbon-sink target of −310 Mt CO2-eq by 2030, with net removals 42 Mt above the 2016–2018 average. Slovakia’s national target is −504 Kt CO2eq by 2030; its landscape is 49.0% forest (24,005 km²) and 43.1% agriculture (21,126 km²). EU restoration measures should be in place on at least 20% of land areas and 20% of sea areas by 2030, and in all ecosystems needing restoration by 2050. EU-wide mitigation potentials are 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr from peatland and wetland restoration and 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr from reforestation respecting biodiversity and sustainable forest management. EU agriculture provisions call for 40% of 2023–2027 CAP funding to support climate objectives, at least 25% of annual Pillar I direct payments to be earmarked for eco-schemes, and at least 35% of Pillar II funds for environment and climate activities; fertilizer-use efficiency offers 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr in mitigation potential.
